Dear  Candidate,  
 
For  this  round,  we  have  prepared  a  case  study.  Please  follow  the  instructions  and  be  ready  to  present  
the
 
outcome
 
to
 
a
 
technical
 
audience

Data

Engineers.
 
 
Case  study  instructions  
There  is  a  set  of  raw  data  stored  in  an  AzureSQL  database  (credentials  will  be  sent  via  email),  
originating
 
from
 
one
 
of
 
our
 
product’s
 
backend
 
databases.
 
The
 
aim
 
of
 
this
 
case
 
study
 
is
 
to
 
create
 
a
 
star-schema
 
data
 
model
 
that
 
captures
 
end-of-month
 
snapshots
 
over
 
the
 
last
 
2
 
years
 
of
 
product
 
usage
 
metrics,
 
aggregated
 
on
 
a
 
customer-level
 
and
 
linked
 
to
 
a
 
customer
 
dimension
.
 
 
The  customer  dimension  should  only  show  current  customer  data  (SCD  type  1).  Transformations  
should
 
be
 
done
 
using
 
SQL
 
with
 
Views
 
and
 
the
 
final
 
data
 
model
 
persisted
 
as
 
Tables.
 
The  historical  changes  of  the  raw  data  are  captured  with  dw_valid_from  and  dw_valid_to  fields  in  
each
 
table.
 
If
 
a
 
record
 
is
 
deleted,
 
the
 
dw_valid_to
 
is
 
set
 
to
 
the
 
deletion
 
date,
 
and
 
there
 
is
 
no
 
record
 
for
 
the
 
primary
 
key
 
with
 
a
 
current
 
valid
 
period.
 
 
The
 
required
 
raw
 
tables
 
and
 
their
 
keys
 
are
 
listed
 
below:
 
Table  name  Grain  Primary  key  Foreign  keys  
raw.aspnet_profile  customer  user_id  user_id  ->  used  to  join  other  aspnet*  tables  
raw.aspnet_membership  customer  user_id  user_id  ->  used  to  join  other  aspnet*  tables  
raw.domain_group  domain  group  domain_group_id  customer_id  ->  corresponds  to  user_id  in  aspnet*  tables  
raw.domain  domain  domain_id  domain_group_id  
 
One  customer  has  0:N  domain  groups ,  and  each  domain  group  has  0:N  domains .

The  metrics  that  should  be  defined  in  the  semantic  layer:  
Metric  Raw  table(s)  Field  /  Business  logic  
Total  number  of  customers  
aspnet_profile  count(distinct  user_id)  
Total  number  of  domains  
domain  Count(*)  WHERE  is_temp_domains  =  0  AND  domain  is  not  deleted  
Number  of  domains  in  S  package  
domain  Count(*)  WHERE  is_temp_domains  =  0  AND  domain  is  not  deleted  AND  full_subpage_count  <=  500  
Number  of  domains  in  M  package  
domain  Count(*)  WHERE  is_temp_domains  =  0  AND  domain  is  not  deleted   AND  full_subpage_count  >  500  AND  <=  5000  
Number  of  domains  in  L  package  
domain  Count(*)  WHERE  is_temp_domains  =  0  AND  domain  is  not  deleted  AND  full_subpage_count  >  5000  
 
The  Customer  dimension  should  contain  the  follow  fields:  
Dimension  field  Raw  table(s)  Field  /  Business  logic  
Customer  Id  aspnet_profile  user_id  
Customer  create  date  (as  a  date  hierarchy  Year-Month-Day)  
aspnet_membership  MIN(user_create_time)  per  customer  
Customer  cancel  date  (as  a  date  hierarchy  Year-Month-Day)  
aspnet_profile  
 
MAX(dw_valid_to)  for  customers  that  have  no  active  record  in  the  table

sources:
  - name: aspnet
    description: Backend raw data from customers information
    database: dev
    schema: main
    tables:

      - name: aspnet_membership
        description: Has the date when the customer was created
        columns:
          - name: user_id
            description: The unique identifier of a user
          - name: user_create_time
            description: The datetime that the user was created in the system
          - name: dw_valid_from
            description: The timestamp from which the record is valid in the data warehouse
          - name: dw_valid_to
            description: The timestamp until which the record is valid in the data warehouse

      - name: aspnet_profile
        description: Contains details about the customer
        columns:
          - name: user_id
            description: The unique identifier of a user
          - name: address_country_code
            description: The ISO 2 digit country code where the customer is located
          - name: payment_currency
            description: The currency associated with the user payment method
          - name: payment_card_expiration_date
            description: The expiration date for the card
          - name: payment_card_type
            description: The brand of the card
          - name: payment_data_completed
            description: Indicates if the payment method data is complete
          - name: user_language
            description: User language in the application
          - name: wants_newsletter
            description: Indicates if the user wants to receive the newsletter
          - name: company_size
            description: Bins of the company size
          - name: customer_plan
            description: The type of the plan associated with the user
          - name: customer_payment_type
            description: Indicates the payment method associated with the user
          - name: dw_valid_from
            description: The timestamp from which the record is valid in the data warehouse
          - name: dw_valid_to
            description: The timestamp until which the record is valid in the data warehouse

sources:
  - name: domains
    description: Backend raw data for the domain events
    database: dev
    schema: main
    tables:
      - name: domain
        description: Contains the domain events over time
        columns:
          - name: domain_id
            description: Unique identifier of the domain
          - name: domain_group_id
            description: Unique identifier of the domain group
          - name: full_subpage_count
            description: The number of subpages for the domain
          - name: is_temp_domains
            description: A flag to indicate if the domain is temporary
          - name: dw_valid_from
            description: The timestamp from which the record is valid in the data warehouse
          - name: dw_valid_to
            description: The timestamp until which the record is valid in the data warehouse

      - name: domain_group
        description: Associates each domain group with their respective customer
        columns:
          - name: domain_group_id
            description: Unique identifier of the domain group
          - name: customer_id
            description: Unique identifier of a customer
          - name: dw_valid_from
            description: The timestamp from which the record is valid in the data warehouse
          - name: dw_valid_to
            description: The timestamp until which the record is valid in the data warehouse

# Name your project! Project names should contain only lowercase characters
# and underscores. A good package name should reflect your organization's
# name or the intended use of these models
name: 'agentic_dbt_project'
version: '1.0.0'

# This setting configures which "profile" dbt uses for this project.
profile: 'agentic_dbt_project'

# These configurations specify where dbt should look for different types of files.
# The `model-paths` config, for example, states that models in this project can be
# found in the "models/" directory. You probably won't need to change these!
model-paths: ["models"]
analysis-paths: ["analyses"]
test-paths: ["tests"]
seed-paths: ["seeds"]
macro-paths: ["macros"]
snapshot-paths: ["snapshots"]

clean-targets:         # directories to be removed by `dbt clean`
  - "target"
  - "dbt_packages"


# Configuring models
# Full documentation: https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/configuring-models

# In this example config, we tell dbt to build all models in the example/
# directory as views. These settings can be overridden in the individual model
# files using the `{{ config(...) }}` macro.
models:
  agentic_dbt_project:
    # Config indicated by + and applies to all files under models/example/
    example:
      +materialized: view
